title: The Chalkbone Cleaver
notes: content: Marrow's Forge will now grind a chalkbone bar into a cleaver, backed with a shard of cartilage for the edge to hold.
content: Marrow's Forge has started stocking chalkbone bar and cartilage shard, for anyone who would rather buy than dig.

title: The Sunken Ring
notes: content: Something has been living where the tenth ring of the Cartilage Rings should be. The waystation sign was right not to count it.
content: The Tenth Ring keeps a pit south-east of the waystation. It drops unkept marrow every time, and sometimes a lance or a cape cut from itself.
content: A sign stands over the pit. Read it before you go down.

title: Chalkbone Seams
notes: content: Chalkbone seams have turned up in the Cartilage Rings, cores of old bone fused into the chalk.
content: Smelt chalkbone ore at a furnace, with a little chalk lump, for a bar worth carrying home.

title: Faces on the people you talk to
notes: feature: Whoever is speaking now appears in the dialogue box, drawn from their own model and animated while they talk, the way RuneScape has always done it.

fix: A resource node that grew back while you were somewhere else stayed a stump until you logged out. The ward announced the change at the moment it happened, which was a message you had to be standing there to hear.

fix: Harvesting with a staff on your back played an Anatomancy spell for the last swing at a node. The blow that empties something ends the job, and the ward was reporting the job rather than the blow.

title: A map, a steadier camera, and a longer rest
notes: feature: A world map. Press M, click the minimap, or type /map. Drag it about, wheel to zoom, and it marks the banks, altars, furnaces, anvils, ranges, cauldrons, sewing tables and wells, along with anyone near enough to see.
feature: Hold the middle mouse button and move to swing the camera. It does what the arrow key pointing the same way does, and a slow drag turns slowly, which a key cannot.
fix: Characters stopped walking when they stopped moving. The legs kept going on the spot indefinitely, because the check for having arrived compared two positions that never quite met.
fix: The same arithmetic was turning everybody to face east the moment they came to a halt. It read the last millionth of a tile as a direction.

balance: The dead stay dead for at least twenty-five seconds, and most things for thirty. Fifteen was not long enough to pick up what they dropped, and it made every resource sharing ground with a spawn a waste of time.

fix: The bulletin you are reading now. It had stopped appearing after an update, for two reasons: the ward only ever posted one for a content delivery and never for anything hand-made, and the server read this file once when it started and never looked again.

title: Weapons in hand, spells in the air
notes: fix: The level-up notice is a small line at the top. It used to cover your character and half the room for three seconds.
fix: Names and health bars stack instead of sitting on top of one another, and every name is drawn before any bar, so nobody can hide an enemy bar with their own.
feature: Weapons are held properly and are about twice the size. A scalpel you cannot see is a scalpel you do not know you are swinging.
feature: Injection has three motions instead of one — a dart is thrown, a bow is drawn, a blowpipe is blown through — and each of them puts something in the air.

feature: Anatomancy has a cast, a bolt and a sound for each spell. Flesh bolt is hurled underarm, nerve strike snaps out and shakes, bile lance is driven two-handed, vital rend takes hold and pulls apart, and transfuse reaches out and drags back.

feature: Gathering looks like the job it is. You turn to face the node, and you swing an axe at a tree, a pick at a seam, a net over a pool and a gaff into an eel hole, with the tool in your hand while you do it.
balance: Trees are three and a half tiles tall, and the rest of the resource nodes grew with them. A throatwood used to be shorter than the nurse chopping it.
fix: A worked-out node becomes a stump, a broken seam or a picked stem, instead of the same thing drawn slightly fainter.

title: Ring Fauna
notes: content: The Cartilage Rings have more living in them than the two that were counted. Cartilage maggots and chalk moths work the seams; a lapsed orderly and something called a ring howler work the maggots and moths.
content: Chalk moth dust and chalk spurs can both be picked off what you kill out there.

title: The Throat in three dimensions
notes: feature: The ward is drawn as a place rather than as a picture of one. The floor rises and falls, everything standing on it is a model, and the light comes from somewhere.

feature: The camera turns. Arrow keys orbit and tilt it, the wheel pulls it in and out, and the compass on the minimap puts it back on north. The map still reads north-up whichever way you are facing.
feature: Every click leaves a mark on the tile it landed on — yellow for going somewhere or using something, red for attacking.
fix: Clicks on the shop and bank windows were falling through to the ward behind them and walking you off mid-purchase. The interface layer had taken an element id the windows were already using.
fix: Your character faces what it is fighting. It also holds what it is fighting with, which it had never done.
fix: A dropped item lies on the floor as itself. Every drop in the game used to be the same grey lump.
fix: Doors open away from whoever is pushing them instead of rotating into the wall.
balance: The old flat view is still there under Settings, for anything that cannot run the new one.

title: Tools that do something
notes: fix: The suture needle, the pestle and mortar and the ward hammer did nothing at all. They were sold, forged and described as tools, and no bench ever asked for them.

balance: The anvil, the cauldron and the sewing table now want the right tool in your pack, as Smith Marrow has been saying all along. The furnace and the range still do their own work. All three tools are on Sceld's shelf for pocket money.
fix: The make window says which tool a bench wants before you click, not after.
fix: An item's tooltip says what its tool is for. "Used for gathering" was vague at best and wrong for the needle.
fix: The skills guide names the tool each resource needs — the bile gaff is for eel holes at Leeching 28, which was until now something you had to find out by owning one and wondering.

title: Sister Ambrose keeps her chapel
notes: fix: There were two Sister Ambroses. One kept the Chapel of the Uvula; the other stood in the Guild of Physicians in Vellumhaven, among the cauldrons. She would start the Long Vigil from there and then tell you to keep watch at the altar “here”, in a room that has never had one. There is one of her now, in the chapel, where the quest says she is.
fix: The Long Vigil asks for three watches in three places, one of them “not in a chapel at all” — and no such altar existed. Every one in the Throat stood in one of the two chapels.
content: A shrine on the Gullet Road, between the braziers: an altar, two graves and a sign. Somebody keeps the candles lit.
balance: The Long Vigil counts places, not altars. Three of them stand in the Uvula chapel and praying at all three was never what Ambrose meant.

title: The Cartilage Rings
notes: content: The map has grown. East of the Larynx Deep, past the cave road, the Throat opens into the Cartilage Rings — pale ribs of the stuff, standing in rows.
content: Two things live out there: ring gnawers, and whatever a chondral warden used to be. Neither is for a nurse who is still counting their first hundred.
content: Cartilage seams can be mined at Delving 45 for shards. The chondral wardens drop a splint worth carrying.
content: A waystation stands on the road in. It has a bed and a brazier and nobody in it.

title: The Sounding
notes: content: New quest — The Sounding. Sister Lull keeps a listening post in the Larynx Deep, south of the cave road. She has been there long enough to stop hearing it.
content: The post is on the map now, with a bed, a brazier and somebody in it.
content: Ward deafeners can be earned from the quest — a hood for anyone working where the Throat is loud.

title: Trading, and a bulletin board
notes: feature: Nurses can trade with each other. Click another nurse, or type /trade <name>. They have to ask you back before anything opens, the way it always worked.
feature: The trade has two screens. Offer, both accept, then a confirmation showing exactly what is about to change hands — and any change at all sends you both back to the first screen.
feature: Offered items leave your pack and are held until the trade settles. Declining, walking apart, dying or logging out all give them straight back.
feature: This bulletin. It appears once when the ward has changed, and /patch brings it back.
content: The ward can now take deliveries — new creatures, kit, recipes, quests and places arrive as content packs without the game being rebuilt around them.

title: Walking, tooltips and skill guides
notes: fix: Nurses walk instead of sliding. Arms and legs swing in opposition, and which foot leads alternates properly even at a run.
feature: Hovering an item shows what it is, where it is worn, what it does, what it is worth, and — in red — any requirement you cannot meet.
feature: Clicking a skill opens what it unlocks, level by level, read straight from the game's own data.

title: Friends, whispers and coloured chat
notes: feature: A friends list that tells you who is on shift, and tells them when you arrive.
feature: Whispers — /tell <name> <message> and /r to reply. Names with spaces go in quotes.
feature: Chat effects. Prefix a message with a colour and a motion: rainbow:wave:the ward is bleeding. /effects lists them all.
fix: A save written the instant before a reconnect can no longer be read back stale.

title: Sound, animation and slower resources
notes: feature: Music that follows you between regions, and sound effects for everything the ward does. All of it synthesised at runtime; there is not an audio file in the repository.
feature: Attack animations for nurses and for the things attacking them, gathering animations, and doors that swing.
balance: Gathering and node respawn take meaningfully longer. Resources were popping back before you had walked away.

title: The ward opens
notes: feature: Throatscape moves onto the server. Accounts, passwords and saved progress, one authoritative world, and everybody in it at once.
